data.body:
RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1 — proven, runtime-confirmed). Disposition: ESCALATE (fix requires a design decision on the error-code vocabulary; no code changed).

PROVEN ROOT CAUSE (corrects this ticket's stated Mechanism)
The two cited reproductions (render_workflow, get_workflow_status) do NOT go through
`_mcp_llm._structured_llm_failure`. Those are READ_ONLY tools in `_mcp_reads.py` with no
try/except; their exceptions flow through the GENERIC MCP error guard
`_mcp_errors._envelope_error` -> `rebar._errors.error_code_for`. The real mechanism:

- `WorkflowError` and `WorkflowParseError` (src/rebar/llm/errors.py:114-118) are declared
  subclasses of `LLMError`. They are the workflow engine's DSL parse/lint/migrate/execute/
  lookup error base -- NOT availability errors.
- `render_workflow("nonexistent-wf")` raises `WorkflowParseError("... not found ...")`
  (runs.py:85); `get_workflow_status("nonexistent-run")` raises
  `WorkflowError("unknown run_id ...")` (runs.py:515).
- `error_code_for` (src/rebar/_errors.py:141-142) has a blanket branch 6:
  `isinstance(exc, LLMError) -> "llm_unavailable"`. These workflow errors set no
  `error_code` attribute, so branch 5 does not fire and every workflow caller-input/
  not-found error collapses to `llm_unavailable`.

PROOF (runtime, worktree at origin/main dddaa606):
    render_workflow  -> error_code_for = llm_unavailable
      envelope: {'error':'llm_unavailable','input':'','message':"nonexistent-wf: workflow
                 'nonexistent-wf' not found ..."}
    get_workflow_status -> error_code_for = llm_unavailable
      envelope: {'error':'llm_unavailable','input':'','message':"unknown run_id
                 'nonexistent-run': no run-index entry and no ticket_id given"}
These envelopes match the ticket's reproductions exactly. The MCP envelope shape is
{error,input,message} (no resolution_class/retryable/diagnostic) -- confirming the path is
error_code_for, not _structured_llm_failure. `_structured_llm_failure` is a SECOND,
independent hard-coded `"error":"llm_unavailable"` site (used by review_code/verify_completion/
review_plan); it shares the defect class but is not the path for the two cited repros.

DEFECT ORIGIN (caused_by): ticket 8a31 = biomedical-upper-tench (8a31-e1c3-cf31-4239),
commit 77f1c4011c83 "8a31: MCP failures get CLI's structured error id". That change created
the structured-MCP-error obligation and shipped `error_code_for` with the blanket
`LLMError -> llm_unavailable` mapping without carving out the workflow caller-input/not-found
subclasses (its own message even notes "_mcp_reads/_mcp_llm: the two return-shaped soft errors
gain a code"). Close-class: plan_defect.

LEGITIMACY: defect (standing intent). The structured-identity contract
(docs/mcp-reference.md "Failure shape": `error` drawn from `rebar.KNOWN_ERROR_CODES`) is set
by biomedical-upper-tench; wolflike-chevroned-haddock and dear-name-ladle are the same
"non-availability failure misclassified as llm_unavailable" defect class, both closed fixed.

WHY ESCALATE (not auto-fix). Satisfying AC1/AC2/AC4 requires ADDING new member(s) to the
exported `rebar.KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` vocabulary (also common.schema.json + docs/mcp-reference.md
"Failure shape") -- a contract/schema/API surface change -- and a genuine taxonomy tradeoff:
`WorkflowError` is the base for parse/lint/migrate/EXECUTE errors, and a workflow execution
step can genuinely fail on LLM unavailability, so a blanket `WorkflowError -> not_found` would
regress AC3. The correct design (which new code name(s): workflow_not_found vs not_found vs
invalid_input; whether to introduce finer-grained not-found/caller-input exception subtypes or
set `error_code` attrs on just the not-found/parse sites; and whether `_structured_llm_failure`
should derive its code from error_code_for) is a new design decision. No ADR prescribes it.

SIBLINGS/RESIDUAL: `_structured_llm_failure` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:21-37) hard-codes
`llm_unavailable` for the LLM-tier tools; the same fix should route it through the chosen
classification so AC4 holds there too. No fix landed; no worktree retained beyond this session.
